request: How is the Highway Trust Fund financed, and when is it projected to run short of money?

reply.reply:
**The Highway Trust Fund is financed mainly by federal motor-fuel taxes, with general-fund transfers historically used to keep it solvent; CBO projections suggest payment delays could begin in FY2027 for transit and FY2028 for highways without further action.**

- Federal transportation programs are largely financed by motor-fuel taxes deposited into the HTF, with Treasury general-fund transfers used since 2008 to keep it solvent. (R47573, PDF p. 2)
- CBO projects an average annual gap of roughly $33 billion between dedicated surface transportation revenues and spending from FY2027 to FY2031. (R47573, PDF p. 9)
- CBO projects the FTA would possibly pay obligations through the second quarter of FY2027 and FHWA through the first quarter of FY2028. (R47573, PDF p. 11)
- Gasoline/gasohol is taxed at 18.3 cents per gallon and diesel at 24.3 cents per gallon; both rates reduce to 4.3 cents per gallon after September 30, 2028. (R48948, PDF p. 4)
reply.reasoning: CRS explains the main revenue source and use of general-fund transfers, and reports when projected balances may no longer cover obligations by account. CRS also estimates an average annual revenue-versus-spending gap of roughly $33 billion from FY2027 to FY2031.
